text:
Situation: Lorazepam injection 2 mg/mL, 1 mL cartridges (NDC 00409198530) from Hospira, Inc. remain in shortage. FDA first posted the shortage on 2018-05-03 and it is still Current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 17 units (3.4 days on hand). Corvale General holds 99 units (14.6 days) and 83 units (12.9 days) of the same strength and size.

Why (FDA record): The Hospira plant (FEI 1925262) received an OAI classification from an inspection ending 2016-06-08, 694 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued 2017-02-14, 443 days before posting. A later inspection ending 2018-08-15 was classified OAI with a classification letter dated 2020-04-22.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low. Corvale General can spare a small quantity without dropping below two weeks. Alternate products from Hikma and Hospira are FDA-listed Current and have prior pharmacist approvals for concentration or vial-size changes.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 4 units of 2 mg/mL, 1 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director with controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V).
2. Procure lorazepam 2 mg/mL from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. — approved by pharmacist; dose and volume recalculation and verification required.
3. Procure lorazepam 2 mg/mL from Hospira, Inc. (alternate presentation) — approved by pharmacist; dose and volume recalculation and verification required.

Not recommended: Purchase from Civica, Inc. — not on FDA shortage list and no identifiable plant for supply assessment.
